title: Token-aware probe dampening and progressive readiness decay to prevent autoscaler thrash during multi-region failovers
creator: Lena Mitchell
description:
Problem: During regional failovers (planned or sudden), health probe storming and aggressive readiness flips create large, simultaneous capacity churn. This causes the autoscaler to overshoot/undershoot and thrash, producing SLO regressions (p95 latency and error rate spikes). Existing readiness/liveness knobs are too coarse: they act per-pod with static thresholds and cannot account for request token shape or global fanout of probes across regions.

Goal: Implement a probe dampening system that is token-aware and region-aware and a progressive readiness decay state (soft-fail) for pods so that during failover we limit probe fanout, reduce admission sharply but recover gradually, and provide advisory signals to the autoscaler instead of hard triggers. The combined changes should keep availability and latency within SLOs while preventing autoscaler thrash during multi-region failover and load spikes.

Approach overview: 1) Probe fanout limiter: adorn readiness probe layer with a per-region, token-weighted probe budget. Each pod consumes budget based on a measured token/compute score for the in-flight requests it is serving. When budget exhausted, probes are sampled with a configurable drop probability (token-jittered). 2) Token-aware dampening: compute a lightweight token-score per request class (short vs long seq) and prioritize probes for pods serving low-token/latency-critical requests. 3) Progressive readiness decay (soft-fail): when a pod is unhealthy or when region sees elevated failure signals, mark pod into a soft-fail readiness state which reduces admission by a configurable fraction (e.g., 30-70%) rather than full eviction. Stepwise ramp-down/up uses exponential backoff with randomized jitter per-pod to avoid synchronized transitions. 4) Autoscaler advisory channel: readiness transitions emit advisory metrics (readiness_advisory, probe_drop_rate) and an advisory API that the autoscaler can consume to debounce scaling decisions (scale down inhibited when advisory present). 5) Simulation and telemetry: extend existing sim-harness to model token distributions and produce synthetic failovers; add histograms and counters for readiness_state_duration, probe_attempts_by_token_band, and regional_probe_budget_utilization.

Why this is different from prior work: Instead of treating all probes and pods equally, this proposal weights probe behaviour by request token shape and introduces a soft-fail admission state that intentionally trades short-term capacity for stable autoscaler behavior and preserved SLOs. It emphasizes advisory signals to the autoscaler rather than immediate scale actions, aiming to reduce oscillation during region flaps.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumentation: readiness_state transitions, probe_attempts_by_token_band, probe_drop_rate, and regional_probe_budget_utilization are emitted and available in Console dashboards

Sim: Failure simulation with 2-region failover and 2x baseline traffic shows <10% increase in p95 latency compared to baseline and no autoscaler thrash (no more than one unnecessary scaling event per 10 minutes)
Behavior: During synthetic regional outage, average probe fanout per-pod reduces by >60% while total available capacity stays within 85% of expected degraded target using soft-fail admission
Autoscaler: Autoscaler respects advisory channel and delays scale-downs until advisory clears; verified in integration test cluster
Rollback: Feature can be toggled off by feature-flag per-region and per-cluster and we have a documented kill-switch playbook
tasks: Design probe budget algorithm (token-weighted) and edge cases for cold start pods
Implement probe fanout limiter and sampling logic in readiness layer
Add soft-fail readiness state and transition controller with backoff + jitter
Expose advisory metrics and lightweight advisory API for autoscaler
Extend sim-harness to support token-distribution-driven failover scenarios
Create dashboards and alerting for probe_drop_rate and readiness_advisory retention
Run staged canary (eu-west-1, 10% traffic) and monitor for 48h
Document operational runbook and rollback steps
notes: Probe budget heuristics: start with 100 probe-tokens/region/sec and cost = max(1, tokens/256) per probe invocation; tune from canary
Soft-fail admission values: default 50% admission; expose as runtime config per service class
Autoscaler integration: advisory flag should be additive (do not force downscale) and carry TTL of 60s
Edge cases: handle long tail requests and model-compiler cold starts by exempting newly-launched pods from immediate dampening for the first 30s
Telemetry retention: keep readiness_advisory at 1m granularity for 30d for postmortem analysis
